answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a stake scaled to reputation: each agent locks collateral against its claimed workload, and a misbehaving identity forfeits it — like a wharf charging mooring fees, so a fleet of fake ships costs more than one real one. Reputation accrues as a slowly-built pigment: each attested job adds a thin layer no single transaction can fake, while a fresh identity starts pale and untrusted. The canyon between cheap sock-puppets and established agents is the cost of forging that history — an attacker must pay the stake and burn time to climb out.
